Chicago, USA, November 13-17, 2023 Agenda Item: 8 Document for: Discussion and Decision Introduction This document summarizes the discussions on preparing the CR for TR 37.985 on NR_SL_enh2-Core. [Post-115-37.985-NR_SL_enh2-Core] Email discussion and endorsement on Rel-18 draft CRs by Oct 20 – Editors Editors to prepare updated draft CRs by Nov 27 (Monday) Endorsements by Nov 30 (Thursday) First round discussions First a reminder that this TR 37.985 “Overall description of Radio Access Network (RAN) aspects for Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) based on LTE and NR”: Is for V2X features, which in Rel-18 are SL coexistence and SL CA. Is not for general sidelink features, e.g. those intended for commercial use. Hence SL-U is not included. Is a ‘stage-2 like’ TR to be transposed by OPs, and intended primarily for external organizations (hence the 9xx numbering) such as 5GAA to understand 3GPP V2X technology without diving deeply into our TSs. By contrast, internal 3GPP TRs, in the 8xx numbering, are not transposed. Is typically updated approximately once per Release, in time to declare the related core-part WI 100% complete. The additions on bands are taken from TS 38.101-1 and TS 38.101-3. This section summarize the first round email discussions on draft CR v00. Companies are encouraged to provide the first round views by November 28 (Tuesday), 18.00 UTC, then we can update the draft CR accordingly for the next step discussions. Conclusion There were no comments to the draft CR, which was thus endorsed. The final CR is in R1-2312794. [Tables] Table 1: Company | View

{"chunk_id":"R1-160563-001","collection":"ran1_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Samsung"],"tdocNumber":"R1-160563","title":"Discussion on PUCCH for UL LAA"},"point_id":"13720923788458854441"}
In RAN 70 meeting, the work item on enhanced LAA has been approved [1]. The detailed objectives of the work item are to specify support for the following functionalities: UL carrier aggregation for LAA SCell(s) (with one or more UL carriers in unlicensed band) using Frame Structure type 3 [RAN1, RAN2, RAN4] The channel access mechanism shall use the decisions made in RAN1 during Rel-13 as a starting point Specify support for PUSCH and SRS Support both self-scheduling and cross-carrier scheduling from licensed spectrum. If needed, specify support for PUCCH [RAN1] If needed, specify support for PRACH [RAN1] The work item should also specify base station and UE core requirements of 5 GHz spectrum to support the above features [RAN4, RAN1] Complete support for 10 MHz system bandwidth as an LAA SCell [RAN4] In this contribution, we discuss the issues of PUCCH. First of all, the necessity of supporting PUCCH transmission on unlicensed band is discussed. Then, the potential standard impact of PUCCH is analyzed.

At first a summary of the requirements that are further explained in section 3: A. TEI Work Item codes shall only be used for small technical enhancements and improvements. B. A TEI CR set shall be fully completed within one TSG cycle/quarter in all affected WGs. C. TEI Work Item codes shall not be used where another appropriate Work Item code exists. D. Inter-TSG aspect: D1. Normally, for TSG SA/CT work that requires cat.B/C CRs from RAN WGs a RAN WI is required. D2. In case the RAN work triggered via a TSG SA/CT WI* is small and it affects only one RAN WG, then the RAN WG CR(s) shall use the WI code* of the TSG SA/CT WI that triggered this work. *NOTE: provisional WI codes, companion WIDs/"mini-WIDs" are not meant here but already TSG approved proper WIs. D3. It is not possible to trigger work in RAN WGs via TEI CRs coming from TSG SA/CT or SA/CT WGs. The same applies for the reverse direction. Cases identified by the RAN WGs have to be reported to TSG RAN and the affected TSG (SA or CT) stating that an SA/CT WI is required for RAN to undertake the work. E. Inter-RAN WG aspects: E.1 It is mandatory to fill out the "other specs affected" field for all CRs, i.e. either Yes or No shall be ticked and if Yes is ticked all TSs/TRs impacted by each CR shall be indicated, referring to the exact CR numbers to those TSs/TRs and this for the present WG and all other WGs that have CRs linked to the present CR. TEI CRs missing this information or having wrong information shall not be approved. Exception: for test specifications mentioned in the "other specs affected" field, it is not required to mention CR numbers. E.2 Each TEI cat.B/C CR and each TEI cat.F/A CR that corrects functionality related to an earlier TEI cat.B/C CR shall have a unique TEI identifier in square brackets [ ] at the end of the CR title on the CR cover sheet. TEI cat.B/C CRs and follow-up TEI cat.F/A CRs without such a unique TEI identifier cannot be approved at RAN. The usage of [ ] in CR titles for other purposes than TEI identifiers shall be avoided as they may be interpreted as TEI identifiers. TEI identifiers are strings (max. 18 characters or less) composed of letters (upper and/or lower case), digits (0..9) and underscores (_). The usage of hyphens should be avoided. No blanks or special characters (like e.g. :;.,!?<>"£%^&*(){}+=@#~'/\|) shall be used in TEI identifiers. A TEI identifier is case sensitive (i.e. [ABCDE] and [abcde] are different TEI identifiers). However different TEI identifiers that differ only by case shall not be used. Follow-up TEI cat.F/A CRs require the same unique TEI identifier as the original cat.B/C CRs. If TEI crosses WG boundaries, all impacted WGs have to use the same unique TEI identifier. E.3 WG chairs reports report to TSG RAN about all agreed and technically endorsed cat.B/C TEI CRs and all follow-up cat.F/A CRs of the last quarter, i.e. all CRs with TEI identifiers. This means that for each unique TEI identifier all related CRs of the considered WG are listed with spec, CR number, rev number, REL, category, RAN Tdoc number, WG Tdoc number, CR title, version and WI code. For each TEI identifier a clear statement is required that clarifies the impacts on other RAN WGs: - no impact on other WGs - potential impacts on WGx: <optional explanation of the impact> - impact on WGx: spec number and/or WG Tdoc number E.4 MCC will support this tracking activity with a list of TEI CRs that were handled at RAN and that have unique TEI identifiers.

t.B/C TEI CRs have to be completed within one quarter, this is time critical. Therefore very good preparation of cat.B/C TEI CRs which affect multiple WGs is essential. To E.2: This principle was endorsed in RP-202867 [7] and further guidance for this approach is provided here: - The originating company takes care that related CRs in other WGs and follow-up TEI cat.F/A CRs in later meetings use the same TEI identifier as the original cat.B/C CR. - Unique identifiers are not added retroactively: cat.F/A CRs to former cat.B/C TEI CRs which did not have a unique TEI identifier (because the cat.B/C CR was written before RAN #92e) will not get a unique TEI identifier. - Apart from plain TEI CRs, the unique TEI identifiers shall also be applied to NR_newRAT-Core, TEIxx CRs because NR_newRAT-Core was the huge WI for 5G. - As the unique identifiers are part of the CR title, they will be automatically stored in the CR database. Therefore CR authors have to make sure that the complete CR title in 3GU is in line with the title on the CR cover.
